title: Meta Content Library Community Roundtable: Where to for Social Media Research?
snippet: Conference announcement listing Fabio Giglietto as an expert panelist at the 2026 Social Media & Society Conference's Roundtable. He joined other leading computational social scientists to discuss the practicalities and challenges of doing research using the newly mandated Meta Content Library (MCL) under EU regulations.
description: Fabio Giglietto is featured as a panelist for the 'Meta Content Library Community Roundtable' at the International Conference on Social Media & Society 2026.

title: Secondo uno studio dell'università di Urbino l'algoritmo di Facebook ora punisce la politica ufficiale e premia gli estremisti antieuropei. Pd e FdI verso una legge bipartisan sulle piattaforme
snippet: This report details Giglietto's extensive research analyzing over 2.5 million Facebook posts. The news highlights how his findings—showing a 72% reach reduction for mainstream parliamentarians alongside relative growth for extremist groups—sparked calls from Italian political parties for bipartisan regulatory legislation of digital platforms.
description: National news coverage highlighting how Fabio Giglietto's University of Urbino study on Facebook's algorithm prompted Italian political parties to propose bipartisan regulations for big tech.

Algoritmi e democrazia: il caso Meta secondo lo studio Uniurb che ha avviato un'interrogazione al Parlamento europeo
snippet: An official press release and news coverage by the University of Urbino detailing how Fabio Giglietto's study, 'A Pretty Blunt Approach,' sparked critical political debate. It explains the study's findings on algorithmic filtering, how it was highlighted on the investigative TV program 'Report' (Rai3) on April 12, 2026, and how it inspired an official inquiry in the European Parliament.
description: An official press release from the University of Urbino detailing how Prof. Fabio Giglietto's research on Meta's algorithms led to an official European Parliament inquiry and a European Commission investigation under the Digital Services Act.
